descriptionHtml:
Bug B18 · P1 · known

Many dates and times follow the device clock instead of server time (UAT 3.8): 'NEW TODAY', admit date, vitals date, task done time, transcript date; with a phone two days slow a held drug is stamped two days back and the next cleanup deletes it

Tickets: TFA-92584 ready for qa (UAT 3.8); TFA-92597 ready for qa (R6); TFA-92579 AC 3/4 ready for qa (NEW TODAY); TFA-94745 ready for qa (draft restore) · counts as a QA bug: yes · found on: local

Note: Root cause known (Daniela asked for server time on 10-03); the deleted drug, missing badge and wrong draft restore are new symptoms. TC-16/S18 (UAT 3.8, one device set to the wrong date): a phone a day ahead files its bedside line in a row dated tomorrow on the shared record, and the next write from a correctly clocked device lists the lines before it twice (the transcript archive trusts the device date). Which calendar day a correct device should use when its local day and the server's UTC day differ is the open question Q9 (D10); TC-16/S25 passed otherwise. Review 2026-10-14 (TFA-92579/92584): a browser whose day is ahead writes the badge roll back to the server, and every device shows Follow-up, with the matching template and billing family (TC-01/S08, TC-20/S20a; TFA-92584 AC 8). The failing cell of TC-25/S24a is the card's NEW TODAY, which compares addedAt with the device's date (PatientCard.tsx:154-156). EFS/S28 (a)(b) restore drafts by the device date (TFA-94745); (c), an old draft put in today's box, is B13's. Review 2026-10-15 (TFA-94514): the analytics day is the device date too (pilotUsageEvents / pilotDailyRounding use localDay()): a phone 3 days ahead files its rows under its own day, and an encounter across the phone midnight is split over two days and never timed (OAT-06/S10).

Other cases of the same bug (counted once): TC-01/S08, TC-10/S22, TC-19/S19, TC-22/S23, TC-25/S24a, TC-02/S13b, EFS/S28, TC-16/S18, TC-06/S19, OAT-06/S10, TC-06/S23, TC-21/S22, TC-25/S24b, TC-19/S23

Approach · TC-12 Important Points · S23 Wrong browser clock (48 h behind, or +13 h in another time zone): points neither vanish nor take the device's time

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U8 The expiry clock uses server time, not device time: a phone with a wrong date, no clock set, or another time zone shows the same points as any other device. (UAT 3.8; TFA-94699 AC 7) — gate: blocked: TFA-94699 in progress
  • U5 Points expire 12 h after they were written; a point checked 13 h after it was written is gone (Hospital 3.6: Important Points 12 h; TC-12 step 6 repeats it in Nursing Home). … (UAT TC-12; UAT 3.6; TFA-92590 AC 6; TFA-94699 AC 2) — gate: blocked: TFA-92590 in progress
  • U3 Re-saving the pre-round note with different content leaves every point untouched: Save Note never adds, edits, or removes a point. (UAT TC-12; TFA-92590 AC 2; TFA-92590 description) — gate: blocked: TFA-92590 in progress
  • U7 Every step is repeated in Nursing Home and must pass in both modes. (UAT TC-12; UAT 3.3; TFA-92590 AC 3) — gate: blocked: TFA-92590 in progress

Test design technique: Device (device) — Look at the layout and gestures at phone size or on a real device (iPhone / Pixel).

Given Local stack; Playwright contexts with the same account: one with clock.setSystemTime(now - 48 h), a variant with timezoneId 'Pacific/Kiritimati' and the clock +13 h, and one with the normal clock

When In each mode, in the wrong-clock context: add a point, Save Note, open and close the editor, reload. Then open the same chart in the normal-clock context

Then The point is present in both contexts after every step; the stored points clock is server time

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): UAT 3.8, TFA-94699 AC 7 (clocks use server time). Judged: the point is listed in both contexts after add, Save Note, open/close and reload; an admin read shows ptsEditedAt within +-2 min of the server's time:now. Main writes ptsEditedAt from the browser (buildReviewedNotePatch, usePreRoundProcess, PreRoundNotesCard, Nursing Home closeEditor and handleProcess all use Date.now() …

Where it ran: local newspec-b (new Playwright specs); test method PW · Playwright script; lane planned in the matrix: existing tests (Tim's Playwright) (blocked)

S23 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/TC-12.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Triage (2026-10-14): 1 row.

Issue type: Known product issue · environment local · tickets TFA-92590 in progress; TFA-94699 in progress

On a phone whose clock is 48 h behind, a newly added Important Point is stamped as 48 h old and is deleted from the chart on every device at the next lifecycle pass. In Nursing Home, the pre-round text saved with that clock is also gone after a reload.

Evidence: allure e88a7b99: ptsEditedAt is stored on the device clock (-2880 / +780 min vs the server). OAT-04 knownGaps K10 already records that retention clocks are stamped with the browser clock (TFA-94699 AC 7, in progress). The S23 oracle expected this fail, and TC-12 risks list it. With the Kiritimati +13 h clock the points survive.

Environment: local — main e02167f, local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane newspec-b.

Test method: PW · Playwright script; secondary: CODEREVIEW · Code review — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on both; Source: newspec-b.

UAT item: TC-12 Important Points · Section: A2 · Pre-Round · Scenario: TC-12/S23

Wrong browser clock (48 h behind, or +13 h in another time zone): points neither vanish nor take the device's time

Tickets: TFA-92590 Important Points (in progress); TFA-94699 Data Retention & Purge (in progress)

New local lane newspec-b: status failed in newspec-b/results.json → failed · product (failed · product (the lane flagged a product issue)).

How it is tested (newspec-b/plan.json, automatable: yes): Chromium spec, fresh account, contexts: clock now−48 h; timezoneId Pacific/Kiritimati with clock +13 h; normal. In each mode add a point, Save Note (parse answered at the socket), open/close editor, reload; then open the chart in the normal context; read ptsEditedAt via the chart query and compare with server time (time:now if callable). — Device clock via Playwright; parse mocked so the run is about the clock, not the model.

Detail:

Re-run 17:10. Hospital −48 h: the point is stored on add, Save Note and open/close with ptsEditedAt −2880 min vs server; it is deleted by the next lifecycle pass (in this run the wrong-clock page's own reload ran it) and the normal-clock context shows nothing. Nursing Home −48 h: the point is kept and shown in both contexts, but stamped 48 h old (−2880 min), and the NH pre-round text saved under that clock was '' after the reload. Kiritimati +13 h (saved session refused, signed in again; see _observations): points survive in both modes and both contexts, but ptsEditedAt is +780 min vs server. Every run stores ptsEditedAt on the device clock (oracle: within ±2 min of server time).

Product issue: Hospital: a physician whose phone clock is two days behind adds 'QA-CLOCK check telemetry'; it is stamped 48 h old and deleted at the next lifecycle pass, so it disappears from the chart for everyone. Nursing Home: the point is kept but stamped 48 h old, and the NH pre-round text saved under that clock was gone after reload. A clock 13 h ahead stamps points 13 h in the future (they outlive their expiry). Breaks TC-12 U8 (UAT 3.8, TFA-94699 AC 7: clocks use server time). Cause: ptsEditedAt is written from the browser's Date.now().

Evidence: 4 attached.

Dev run: skipped: local-only — local-only — Lane A (our scripted spec, not written yet): page.clock / timezoneId browser contexts on a fresh local account, plus an admin read of ptsEditedAt and time:now; dev has no admin key, so it runs on the local stack only (Quinn 2026-10-14).. This local result replaces that dev entry (the scenario appears once).
